description: Historical patterns remain broadly useful and existing risk models perform adequately.
AI cyber automation platforms biotechnology and data infrastructures change risk faster than governance adapts.
Climate hazards intensify faster than infrastructure insurance public health and planning systems adapt.
Conflict sanctions supply disruption institutional rivalry and bloc formation increase uncertainty.
Debt stress liquidity pressure asset repricing or confidence collapse spreads across institutions.
Public agencies governance systems or coordination mechanisms lose capacity or legitimacy.
Multiple risks interact across climate finance technology infrastructure health and politics.
Institutions develop monitoring trigger points learning loops and public accountability for uncertainty.
